AUTHOR: Martija
TITLE: SynDHN: Multi-Object Fish Tracker Trained on Synthetic Underwater Videos
DATA: Own underwater videos from sites across the Philippines (detector annotations from Labao & Naval); synthetic MOT dataset (6 sites, 3000 train frames) for DHN training; 4 manually annotated real test videos (450 frames) from other sites
V_EV: Table I/III site conditions: 'Site5 partial coral background, heavy marine snow'; Sec III-A: 'Each site has different water, illumination, hue, and background conditions'
D2: train: synthetic 3000 frames (6 sites) + val; test: 4 real videos, 450 frames, from different sites
D_EV: Sec IV-C: 'We take 4 underwater videos taken from sites that are different from the sites we used in generating our synthetic dataset.'
R_EV: Sec III-A: 'The data used in this paper is composed of several underwater videos taken in different locations across the Philippines.' Test sites from same video collection
C_EV: Sec IV-D / Table IV: evaluation uses 'Identity Switches (IDs) [47] because they encompass identity preservation'; IDs reported per tracker (e.g., 290 for Sp-App+SynDHN)
E_EV: Sec IV-D: 'we only focus our evaluation on ... the IDF1 Score [46], the Multi-Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) and Identity Switches (IDs)'
ARCH: Faster R-CNN (ResNet-50 FPN) + repurposed Deep Hungarian Network affinity estimator (spatial + appearance cues); baselines Tracktor, SORT
NOTE: Train on synthetic videos made from fish blobs of the same Philippine video campaign; test on real videos from different sites of the same campaign -> R1=N per P2 (synthetic-to-real gap not counted as external). Detector pre-trained on Labao & Naval annotations; overlap of detector training data with test sites not stated (check D).
